derivation: The rule fails where p*q > 5.8: a hyperbola, curved in both axes and asymptotic to each. Closed form over the square [0.5, 2.5]^2 of area 4: with b = 2.5 and c = 5.8 the set {pq > c} has area b^2 - c + c(ln c - 2 ln b) = 6.25 - 5.8 + 5.8(1.757858 - 1.832581) = 0.0166, so 0.42% of the domain - within a factor of two of synthetic/one_pct_2d at 0.500%, the axis-aligned narrow rung it is difficulty-matched to. The region enters the square only above p = c/b = 2.32, which is the declared boundary: below it every q is safe, and above it the crossing moves continuously with q, which is what a hyperbola does to an axis-aligned band and what the boundary tolerance of 0.1 admits rather than pretends to pin.
